record.original_question: If N is a non-prime II_1 factor, must its Haar unitaries form a unique sequential commutation orbit?

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Let N be a non-prime II1 factor. Does it have a unique sequential commutation orbit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let (N,τ) be a diffuse tracial von Neumann algebra with separable predual; in particular consider the case that N is a II_1 factor. A unitary u ∈ N is called a Haar unitary if τ(u^n) = 0 for every nonzero integer n. Fix a free ultrafilter ω on ℕ and form the tracial ultrapower N^ω. Two Haar unitaries u, v ∈ N are said to sequentially commute (written u ↔ v) if uv = vu inside N^ω (equivalently in N when both lie in N), and we extend this to an equivalence relation ≈ on the set of Haar unitaries of N by declaring u ≈ v whenever there is a finite chain of Haar unitaries u = w_0, w_1, …, w_k = v in N^ω with w_{i-1} ↔ w_i for each i. The equivalence classes of ≈ are called the sequential commutation orbits of N.

A II_1 factor N is called prime if it cannot be written as a tensor product N ≅ N_1 ⊗̄ N_2 of two II_1 factors; otherwise N is called non-prime.

Question. Suppose N is a non-prime II_1 factor (with separable predual). Must the set of Haar unitaries of N form a single sequential commutation orbit; that is, is there a unique ≈-equivalence class?
artifact.status_search_result: The framework of sequential commutation orbits for Haar unitaries in tracial von Neumann algebras was introduced recently, with a dichotomy showing the equivalence relation has either 1 or uncountably many orbits, and connections to property Gamma and 1-bounded entropy. The specific question of whether every non-prime II_1 factor has a unique sequential commutation orbit is listed as an open problem; no resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Sequential commutation in tracial von Neumann algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces sequential commutation equivalence on Haar unitaries; dichotomy of 1 or uncountably many orbits.
status_evidence.claim: The notion is recently introduced and the orbit-count dichotomy is established, but specific characterization for non-prime II_1 factors is not stated as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Internal sequential commutation and single generation
status_evidence.snippet: Develops applications to single generation; relates orbit structure to property Gamma.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work extends the theory but does not resolve the non-prime case.
